title: Luda Technology, Zhicheng Computing, TuringQ Plan Quantum Computing Deployment
excerpt: Luda Technology’s AI Data Quant Tech signs a strategic cooperation agreement with Zhicheng Computing and TuringQ to advance quantum computing deployment.
content:
Luda Technology Group Limited, a manufacturer and trader of stainless steel and carbon steel flanges and fittings, a trader of coal, and an operations manager in computing infrastructure, announced a strategic cooperation agreement between its subsidiary, Asia AI Data Centre & Quantum Technology Co., Ltd. and Zhicheng Computing and TuringQ to deploy and fund quantum computing initiatives across China, specifically targeting the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area.

According to Luda Technology’s Chief Executive Officer, Ma Biu, “This Agreement advances our efforts to develop an operating platform for AI and advanced computing infrastructure.” The collaboration aims to coordinate procurement, funding and technical expertise for practical quantum computing services.

Asia AI Data Centre & Quantum Technology Co., Ltd. will coordinate procurement and funding for a new quantum computing initiative, a move that represents a significant expansion for Luda Technology Group Limited, which has historically focused on stainless steel flanges, carbon steel fittings and coal trading. to support this expansion into advanced computing. The agreement outlines specific roles for each partner. TuringQ will supply quantum computing equipment and software, including system integration and technical services.

Regular coordination meetings, covering procurement forecasts and facility compatibility, will be essential for implementation, with designated representatives managing day-to-day operations. While the agreement establishes a three-year initial term with automatic renewal, it does not guarantee specific investment amounts or revenue streams, requiring separate agreements for individual projects.

The framework focuses on intentions rather than legally binding commitments to purchase or supply. Ma Biu, Chief Executive Officer of Luda Technology, further emphasized the company’s shift towards practical application, stating, “Our focus is now on the practical work needed to turn computing technology into usable services, from equipment deployment and supporting facilities to ongoing operations.” The collaboration intends to evaluate commercially viable projects, supporting Luda Technology’s diversification beyond its traditional industrial materials business.
